Assessment, intervention, and ethical considerations of artificial intelligence for depression and suicide risk: A scoping review.
desc: [Psychiatry research] Depression and suicidal behavior constitute leading causes of global disease burden. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers promise for improving detection, intervention, and prevention, yet no comprehensive review has simultaneously mapped AI-driven assessment, intervention, and ethical considerations across both conditions. To systematically map AI applications for depression and suicide risk across three thematic axes: (1) assessment and diagnosis, (2) conversational AI and AI-driven interventions, and (3) ethical, equity, and regulatory considerations, and to evaluate translational maturity using a novel framework. Following JBI scoping review methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, six databases were searched from January 2020 through March 2026. Two independent reviewers screened 5079 records using a two-stage process, yielding 2844 included studies (Cohen's kappa = 0.66). Data were extracted using a standardized charting form with AI-assisted full-text analysis. Assessment/diagnosis dominated (n = 1785), with fewer intervention studies (n = 318). Large language model-related studies rose from <1% (2020-2022) to 11.1% (2025) of included studies annually. Translational Readiness Framework classification revealed 44.8% Laboratory, 49.2% Bridge, and 6.0% Clinical stage, with intervention studies showing the highest Clinical-stage proportion (16.7% vs. 5.9% for assessment). Five cross-cutting observations emerged, including an inverted evidence pyramid and persistent cross-axis integration gap (4.4%). Despite technical advances, the evidence base remains concentrated at early translational stages. The proposed Translational Readiness Framework provides a structured lens for evaluating progress and guiding research prioritization. Closing the gap between laboratory promise and clinical impact requires a shift from model-centric to patient-centric research and from benchmark performance to real-world validation.

title: DUNEDepth: Bronchoscopic Depth and Pose Estimation via Hybrid Adaptation of a 3D-Vision Foundation Model
desc: State-of-the-art bronchoscopy guidance systems and computer-aided diagnosis methods have emerged as important tools for early lung cancer detection. Effective use of these tools depends on being able to accurately link a patient's bronchoscopic airway exam video to their pre-operative 3D chest CT scan. Unfortunately, the derivation of such links, which include bronchoscope depth and camera motion, from the exam video remains an open problem. Building on recently proposed 3D-vision foundation models, we propose DUNEDepth, a hybrid architecture that combines a shared DUNE ViT encoder, a twin MASt3R cross-attention decoder structure, and a prediction head that includes elements of the MASt3R and Reloc3r models. To fine-tune the architecture to our application, we utilize an integrated hybrid synthetic-supervised/self-supervised training strategy that draws on both bronchoscopic video and CT-derived virtual bronchoscopic views. Experiments drawing on bronchoscopic video sequences demonstrate that DUNEDepth more accurately derives depth information and camera motion trajectories than previously proposed self-supervised methods.

title: LOTUS: lineage-aware optimal transport reconstructs continuous clonal fate dynamics
desc: Destructive sampling in single-cell sequencing obscures ancestor-descendant relationships, limiting the continuous reconstruction of cell-fate dynamics. Here we present Lineage-aware optimal transport for unbalanced single-cell dynamics (LOTUS), a framework that integrates time-resolved transcriptomic snapshots with clonal lineage information from engineered barcodes or endogenous T cell receptor clonotypes. LOTUS couples clone-level optimal transport with neural unbalanced transport to model continuous cellular state change, population growth and clonal propagation under lineage-consistent constraints. In branching simulations, LOTUS reduced lineage-inconsistent transport relative to benchmark methods, lowering off-target routing from 4.94-14.84% to 1.10%. On LARRY lineage-barcode scRNA-seq of hematopoiesis, LOTUS reconstructed branching trajectories, improved early neutrophil-monocyte fate-boundary prediction, and inferred multi-fate progenitors and fate-biased meta-clones, linking their distinct fate potentials to inferred epigenetic priming. On CellTagging scRNA-seq of fibroblast reprogramming, it distinguished reprogrammed from failed trajectories and prioritized fate-associated perturbation genes. In longitudinal scRNA-seq and TCR-seq of malaria-responsive memory (CD45RA-) CD4+ T cells, it preserved endogenous clonotype structure and reconstructed TR1 dynamics and regulatory networks. LOTUS thus converts lineage-resolved single-cell snapshots into interpretable, continuous models of fate dynamics and their regulatory programs.

title: Updates in cardiovascular CT imaging in 2025: A year in review.
source: PubMed · Journal of cardiovascular computed tomography
desc: [Journal of cardiovascular computed tomography] The year 2025 brought long-term outcome data supporting coronary CT angiography (CCTA)-guided management of stable chest pain, a proposed reframing of coronary artery disease around atherosclerosis rather than ischemia, and the first large-scale real-world evaluation of a national artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled CT-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR-CT) program. This review summarizes selected advances in cardiovascular computed tomography (CCT) published in print or online during 2025. The studies span coronary artery disease outcomes and prevention, quantitative plaque analysis, photon-counting detector CT, coronary artery calcium scoring, pericoronary inflammation imaging, AI and machine learning, structural and congenital heart disease, and consensus and training documents. For each study we summarize the design, principal findings, limitations, and likely clinical implications, and we close with the barriers, including technical standardization, vendor-specific thresholds, equitable access, and the need for randomized outcome trials, that must be addressed before many of these advances can be implemented broadly.

title: Measure Before You Repair: An Explainable Agent for Blind Restoration of Multi-Artifact 3-D MRI
desc: A brain MRI scan can carry an unknown mix of artifacts, so restoration has to be blind, yet most deep-learning methods are built to correct one known artifact. We present Dx-Rx, an agent in which a multimodal large language model (MLLM) measures suspected artifacts before it repairs them. To our knowledge, it is the first agent to restore whole 3-D MRI volumes, whereas earlier MRI agents restore 2-D slices. In a loop, it looks at slices of the 3-D volume, calls five diagnostic tools (noise, spike, ghosting, bias field, motion) and four restoration tools in any order it chooses, checks each repair, can return to any earlier version to change the order, and ends with a radiology-style report of its diagnostic reasons, the repairs it applied and their results. We simulated up to five artifacts on 148 whole 3-D T1-weighted volumes, at levels calibrated to radiologists' grades of real scans. An MLLM that only looked at the image, as earlier MRI agents do, removed at most 19.7 % of the artifact error. With the best of five MLLMs, Dx-Rx removed a mean 64.5 %, nearly matching the 64.6 % of the same tools given the ground-truth artifacts, which are never known for a clinical scan. With all five models, it made no volume worse and was on par with or better than an expert rule-based pipeline built from the same tools (62.3 %). Code and demo are public at https://itu-biai.github.io/measure-before-you-repair.

title: Psychological support for depression and anxiety across chronic illness contexts: a comparative evaluation of three general-purpose AI chatbots.
desc: [Frontiers in psychiatry] Digital mental health tools, including general-purpose artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots, may provide accessible and low-threshold psychological support for people living with chronic conditions. However, their value in this population depends not only on recognizing depression or anxiety, but also on understanding how psychological distress is shaped by disease-specific experiences and when self-guided support should transition toward professional care. We evaluated the appropriateness, contextual sensitivity, safety, and consistency of psychological support provided by three widely accessible AI chatbots across contrasting chronic illness contexts. We conducted a standardized simulated-patient benchmarking study comparing ChatGPT, Gemini, and Doubao. Twenty scenarios were developed across type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU), representing matched mild and moderate presentations of depression and anxiety together with condition-specific distress related to diabetes self-management and CSU-related flare uncertainty. Each scenario was independently submitted to all three systems in two testing rounds, yielding 120 responses. Blinded raters assessed overall psychological support appropriateness, recognition and emotional support, chronic-illness contextualization, psychological support and referral, psychosomatic balance and safety, and major clinical or safety errors. Repeated testing assessed response consistency. Overall psychological support appropriateness differed across systems (P = 0.002), with 90.0% of ChatGPT, 75.0% of Gemini, and 55.0% of Doubao responses meeting the prespecified appropriateness threshold. Recognition and emotional support was consistently strong across systems, whereas greater differences emerged in chronic-illness contextualization (P = 0.001), psychological support and referral (P = 0.002), and psychosomatic balance and safety (P<0.001). All responses to mild presentations were classified as psychologically appropriate, compared with 58.3% of responses to moderate presentations, indicating that performance became less reliable when digital support required stronger escalation toward professional assessment. Contextualization was also less consistent in CSU, particularly when responses needed to incorporate flare unpredictability, pruritus, sleep disruption, and illness uncertainty. Major clinical or safety errors occurred in 0%, 10.0%, and 15.0% of first-round ChatGPT, Gemini, and Doubao r

title: A Guideline-Grounded Multi-Agent Framework for Personalized Exercise Prescription from Clinical and Wearable Data
desc: Translating population-level exercise guidance into individualized prescriptions requires integrating clinical and wearable data, including diagnoses, medications, functional limitations, and baseline activity, with condition-specific recommendations, a process difficult to scale beyond specialist rehabilitation settings. We developed FITTER, a multi-agent framework that integrates these data with condition-specific guidance to generate personalized FITT-VP prescriptions and applies deterministic safety audit and repair to correct rule-checkable violations. We evaluated FITTER using data from 400 All of Us participants (300 cancer, 100 stroke) against five LLM comparators through computational evaluation, ablation, and structured clinician review. FITTER achieved 98.5% safety-constraint compliance versus 75.8-85.8% for comparators and showed greater quantitative dosing precision and guideline alignment. Cancer-cohort ablation identified safety audit and repair as the largest contributor to safety-constraint compliance. Clinicians reviewed 80 prescriptions across safety, personalization, instruction concreteness, anticipated effectiveness, and clinical acceptability. FITTER provides a clinician-facing approach integrating clinical and wearable data, guidance, and explicit safety constraints.

title: Outcomes of informal and formal care models at the end of life: An AI-supported systematic review.
desc: [Geriatric nursing (New York, N.Y.)] Multimorbidity and functional decline become increasingly prevalent with age, particularly in those near the end of life. This poses critical challenges for both families and society in providing adequate care. However, it remains unclear which type of care yields better outcomes. To systematically assess the impact of informal care, formal care, and a combination of both on health outcomes, healthcare utilization, and costs of care for older adults near the end of life. A systematic review with narrative synthesis was registered on PROSPERO (CRD42024512003). Screening was assisted by machine learning tool ASReview, and study quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, with support from large language model TXYZ.AI. Articles published between database inception and June 4th, 2025 were identified in PubMed, Embase, and CINAHL. Thirty-six studies, including 20 observational and 16 interventional were included. Most observational studies examined place of death, with some associations involving informal care pointing towards lower home death or greater hospital death. In contrast, physician and nurse home visits were associated with a greater likelihood of home death. Specialized formal care interventions generally reported improvements in quality of life and reductions in healthcare use. Quality assessment showed 85.2% AI-human agreement, with 44.4% of studies meeting all seven quality criteria. Informal care did not necessarily facilitate home death, whereas formal home-based care was linked to a greater likelihood of home death. Interventional evidence also suggests broader benefits of specialized formal care, although certainty was limited by methodological concerns.

title: Multimodal Prompt Learning with Dual-Granularity Contrastive Alignment for Preoperative Prediction of Lung Adenocarcinoma Invasiveness Using 3D CT
desc: Accurate preoperative prediction of lung adenocarcinoma invasiveness is important for surgical planning and individualized treatment. However, overlapping CT appearances make it challenging to distinguish invasive adenocarcinoma (IAD) from Pre-IAD lesions. We propose a multimodal prompt-learning framework with dual-granularity image-text alignment for 3D CT-based IAD classification. A 3D ResNet-CBAM encoder extracts global and spatial visual features. A frozen RadBERT backbone is adapted with separate learnable prompts for report-level and keyword-level text encoding. These prompts are initialized using semantic representations derived from real-world clinical reports. Global contrastive alignment connects whole-volume CT representations with reports generated from clinician-annotated radiological attributes to provide overall semantic supervision. A multiple instance learning-based local alignment module associates spatial CT features with vascular-focused radiological keywords, to capture local imaging characteristics potentially associated with tumor invasion. The framework jointly optimizes classification and alignment objectives, while inference requires only CT images. Experiments included 1,593 pathologically confirmed nodules. On the test set, the proposed method achieved an accuracy of 87.92%, F1-score of 87.78%, and AUC of 0.9499. Its AUC significantly exceeded that of the image-only Res-CBAM baseline with the same visual backbone (0.9297; DeLong test, p = 0.0078). Ablation analyses supported the complementary contributions of global and local alignment and the benefit of report-based prompt initialization. Qualitative visualizations showed activation within nodules and adjacent vascular structures. These findings suggest that dual-granularity radiological supervision can enhance CT-based invasiveness prediction while preserving a CT-only inference workflow.

title: Artificial intelligence for video-based assessment of surgical performance in robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery in real operative settings: a systematic review.
source: PubMed · International journal of medical informatics
desc: [International journal of medical informatics] Robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery requires specific skills of the surgeon beyond the mastery of conventional laparoscopic techniques. However, efficient and objective methods for evaluating these skills remain limited. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers potential for a more objective, video-based performance assessment. This systematic review aims to evaluate the current evidence of using AI for evaluation of surgical skill in real robotic surgery and outline potential avenues for future research. We systematically searched Ovid Medline, Embase, Clarivate Web of Science, ERIC Institute of Education Sciences and Scopus databases from inception to 10 July 2025, for studies evaluating AI-based technical skill assessment using videos of robot-assisted surgery performed on real patients. Study characteristics, AI approaches, assessment targets, reference standards, and model performance were extracted. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed using PROBAST + AI. Owing to differences in assessment constructs and reported performance measures, findings were synthesised using a structured narrative approach. In total, 2116 articles were identified, of which 5 met our eligibility criteria. AI approaches and assessment targets varied substantially across studies, including prediction of global technical skill scores, analysis of instrument-derived performance metrics, procedure-specific assessment, and surgical error detection. Reference standards included OSATS, GEARS or modified GEARS, PLACE, and procedural experience. Reported performance measures represented different constructs and were not directly comparable across studies. PROBAST + AI identified important methodological limitations, and no study reported external validation using an independent dataset. AI shows potential for video-based technical skill assessment in real robotic surgery, but current evidence is limited and heterogeneous. Future research should prioritise standardised annotation, multicentre intraoperative datasets, and external validation to support reliable translation into clinical practice.

title: State-Aware Virtual Patient Simulation for Training Psychiatrists in Challenging Clinical Scenarios
desc: Psychiatrists must be prepared to manage patients exhibiting challenging psychological states, including suicidal ideation, hallucinations, and other high-risk behaviors. However, opportunities to safely practice such interactions are limited. While recent conversational agents can simulate patients, existing approaches largely rely on large language models (LLMs) to determine patient responses, making it difficult to consistently maintain psychological state, adapt to the clinician's responses, and generate clinically plausible challenges that meaningfully test the clinician. We present a state-aware virtual patient simulation pipeline for training psychiatrists in challenging clinical scenarios. The proposed system maintains an evolving patient state throughout the interaction and orchestrates patient behavior rather than leaving response generation entirely to an LLM. At each interaction, a learning-based behavioral strategy selector determines the type and level of challenge appropriate to the current patient and clinician context. The selected strategy, patient state, clinician response, interaction history, and relevant clinical knowledge are then provided as grounded context to an LLM to generate a semantically relevant and psychologically consistent patient response. Following each session, the system analyzes the interaction and provides feedback to the clinician on their communication and management of the virtual patient.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Laryngology: Applications for Voice, Swallowing, and Endoscopic Assessment.
source: PubMed · ORL-head and neck nursing : official journal of the Society of Otorhinolaryngology and Head-Neck Nurses
desc: [ORL-head and neck nursing : official journal of the Society of Otorhinolaryngology and Head-Neck Nurses] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into otolaryngology-head and neck care, with rapid growth in laryngology due to its reliance on voice analysis, endoscopic imaging, and swallowing assessment. As AI tools move into routine practice, otolaryngology teams play a key role in ensuring ethical, effective, and patient-centered implementation. To describe current and emerging applications of AI in laryngology with direct relevance to otolaryngology-head and neck care. A narrative review of the peer-reviewed literature was conducted, focusing on clinically relevant and investigational AI applications in laryngology care. Areas of emphasis included voice disorders and dysphagia, with attention to nursing, speech language pathology, and surgical practice. AI applications in laryngology care span multiple domains, including automated voice analysis for screening and monitoring, AI-assisted interpretation of laryngoscopy and swallowing studies, noninvasive dysphagia screening using sound or wearable sensors, and tools to support documentation and clinical triage. Collectively, these technologies can improve diagnostic consistency, support earlier identification of complications, and enhance longitudinal monitoring across care settings. Effective integration of AI into laryngeal care requires coordinated team engagement in data analysis, patient education, and clinical decision support. Understanding AI capabilities and limitations is essential for improving care while mitigating bias and supporting efficient workflows. AI-enabled technologies have expanded data-driven laryngology care across voice, swallowing, and endoscopic evaluation. Successful adoption depends on data quality, performance, and workflow integration. Interdisciplinary collaboration and ongoing evaluation of safety and equity can enhance the quality and consistency of laryngeal care.

title: CardioVascBench:Prioritized Diagnosis Generation from Real-World Chinese Cardiovascular Records
desc: Identifying the primary diagnosis alone does not fully characterize a model's diagnosis-generation performance. We introduce CardioVascBench, a retrospective benchmark for prioritized diagnosis generation from real-world Chinese cardiovascular inpatient records. It contains 3,262 de-identified cases, with 2,174 for training and 1,088 for evaluation, linking clinical narratives and textual ECG reports to expert-verified, ordered discharge diagnoses standardized to ICD-10. An English translation of the evaluation set supports aligned cross-lingual comparison. Our evaluation protocol combines terminology normalization and rank-aware scoring to separately assess primary-diagnosis identification, reference-diagnosis coverage, and list precision. Evaluation across 36 systems shows that higher primary-diagnosis accuracy does not necessarily imply higher list precision against discharge references. We also provide CardioKG-Agent, a knowledge-enhanced baseline combining entity normalization, constrained graph retrieval, and guideline evidence. In a staged comparison of three baseline models, supervised fine-tuning plus the agent achieves a 73.5% higher mean composite score than fine-tuning alone, representing a system-level gain. These results measure retrospective agreement with recorded diagnoses; agreement between metric rankings and physician judgments remains to be validated. CardioVascBench supports research on diagnosis prioritization and knowledge-enhanced generation.

title: Thyroid biomarker biosensing: Nanomaterial-enabled electrochemical platforms, clinical translation, point-of-care technologies, and intelligent diagnostics.
desc: [Talanta] Thyroid disorders represent a substantial clinical burden, requiring reliable biomarker measurement for diagnosis, monitoring, and disease assessment. Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), triiodothyronine (T3), thyroxine (T4), thyroglobulin (Tg), calcitonin (CT), and thyroid-associated nucleic acid biomarkers are important analytical targets. Although established immunoassays, ELISA, imaging, and cytological methods remain integral to clinical practice, limitations related to laboratory infrastructure, sample requirements, and workflow complexity have driven the development of alternative analytical platforms. This review focuses primarily on nanomaterial-assisted electrochemical biosensors for thyroid biomarker analysis, examining how nanomaterial properties, biorecognition strategies, and electrochemical transduction influence analytical performance. Metal and metal oxide nanoparticles, carbon nanomaterials, metal-organic frameworks, metal chalcogenides, MXenes, quantum dots, and molecularly imprinted polymers are discussed for their roles in signal amplification, interfacial charge transfer, selectivity, and sensor stability. Complementary approaches, including chemiluminescent, photoelectrochemical, optical, and other emerging sensing strategies, are also considered to contextualize the broader analytical landscape, particularly in relation to their implementation in commercial laboratory and point-of-care platforms for thyroid analysis. Seventy representative analytical and diagnostic systems are comparatively evaluated according to sensing technology, detection range, sample type, and assay time, together with their progression toward portable point-of-care devices, commercial analyzers, rapid diagnostic formats, and wearable platforms. Emerging artificial intelligence and machine learning approaches for signal interpretation, disease classification, and risk assessment are discussed. Challenges in nanomaterial reproducibility, bioreceptor stability, biofouling, matrix effects, fabrication, analytical standardization, external validation, and clinical translation are critically examined. The review identifies key analytical and technological priorities for translating thyroid biosensors from sensitive experimental platforms into robust, reproducible, and clinically relevant diagnostic tools.

title: Polyp Matching Using Deep Learning
desc: A key challenge in colon capsule endoscopy (CCE) analysis is accurately identifying whether multiple images depict the same polyp, which is critical to avoid over-counting and unnecessary clinical interventions. Additionally, this prevents prolonged follow-up colonoscopies where endoscopists search for duplicate polyps without precise localization. This study presents a novel contrastive learning-based approach to polyp matching using a Siamese neural network architecture. The model was trained on a dataset from the Danish CareForColon2015 trial. The dataset comprises 5,103 image pairs of confirmed same polyp and 5,103 pairs of different polyps, annotated by experienced clinicians. The proposed model employs ResNet variants (ResNet18, ResNet34, ResNet50), DenseNet121 and EfficientNet B0/B3 as backbones and utilizes contrastive learning with cosine vector distance metric for classification. Experimental results demonstrate high classification accuracies of up to 92% and AUC values close to 0.98. These results suggest that automated polyp matching has the potential to reduce polyp over-counting, improve patient risk stratification, and reduce unnecessary follow-up colonoscopies.

title: [Ambulatory surgery and enhanced recovery after surgery: advances in concepts and clinical practice].
source: PubMed · Zhonghua yi xue za zhi
desc: [Zhonghua yi xue za zhi] Ambulatory surgery and the concept of enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) are deeply integrated, reshaping the surgical care model. This article systematically reviews and critically analyzes advances in ERAS-driven ambulatory surgery across multiple dimensions, including its current status, the expanding scope of enhanced recovery, and future perspectives. Available evidence shows that ERAS-guided ambulatory surgery not only ensures surgical safety but also significantly shortens hospital stay, reduces medical costs, and improves patient satisfaction. In the future, technologies such as artificial intelligence, wearable devices, and telemonitoring will further promote ambulatory surgery toward individualization, comfort, and intelligence.

title: Improving PI-RADS Prediction and Prostate Cancer Detection from Multiparametric MRI with Anatomical Guidance
desc: Accurate prediction of Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) scores from multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) remains challenging, more so than clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) detection. Given the importance of lesion location in PI-RADS scoring, we evaluated whether incorporating prostate zonal masks improves PI-RADS prediction and csPCa detection across multiple architectures (3D ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and ViT) using a large-scale internal dataset. Anatomical guidance generally improved performance across architectures, with the best results achieved by ResNet-18 with 2-zone guidance for PI-RADS prediction (QWK = 0.511) and ResNet-50 with 5-zone guidance for csPCa detection (AUC = 0.809). Fine-tuned results on external datasets further demonstrated the benefits of anatomical guidance. Furthermore, models with anatomical guidance improved the utility of model-predicted PI-RADS scores for PI-RADS-based csPCa detection (positive defined as PI-RADS>=3). Combining model-predicted and expert-assigned PI-RADS scores significantly increased the AUC from 0.711 to 0.756 (p < 0.05), suggesting that AI-derived PI-RADS scores may provide complementary information to expert assessment for csPCa detection. Overall, our findings highlight the value of incorporating prostate zonal anatomy into deep learning-based prostate MRI assessment.

title: Performance of Deep Learning Algorithms for Segmentation of Shoulder Anatomy on MRI: A Systematic Review.
source: PubMed · Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
desc: [Journal of imaging informatics in medicine] To synthesize the performance and methodological characteristics of fully automated deep learning algorithms for shoulder magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) segmentation. This systematic review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. CENTRAL, PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore were searched from inception through July 17, 2026. The protocol specified fully automated deep learning-based pixel-wise segmentation of shoulder MRI, an expert-derived MRI-space reference standard, and quantitative segmentation metrics. Two reviewers independently screened records; unresolved disagreements were adjudicated by a senior reviewer. Overlapping datasets were linked during synthesis. Of 354 identified records, 169 duplicates were removed, 185 records were screened, and 53 full-text reports were assessed. Thirty-five reports were included (31 journal articles and 4 full conference papers; 2018-2026). U-Net-based encoder-decoder architectures predominated, with additional region-based, transformer, adversarial, and autoencoder approaches. Dice similarity coefficients ranged from approximately 0.81-0.99 for osseous targets, 0.71-0.99 for shoulder muscles, and 0.58-0.94 for tendon or tear regions; intersection-over-union values for tear or surgical-planning regions ranged from 0.45-0.83. MRI protocols and validation designs were heterogeneous, and most reports described retrospective single-center investigations. Five reports used independent external test sets; several others included multicenter images. Overlapping cohorts precluded a valid pooled participant count. Deep learning achieved high accuracy for shoulder bones and rotator-cuff muscles in selected datasets, whereas tear-region performance was more variable. Multicenter patient-level validation and standardized annotation and reporting are needed before routine clinical deployment.

title: DiabAgent: Toward Agentic Physiological Control
desc: As pretraining scales, medical language models have advanced rapidly in clinical question answering. Their ability to achieve effective physiological control through sustained intervention still lacks systematic quantitative evaluation. Type 1 diabetes provides a concrete setting: impaired insulin secretion creates dependence on exogenous insulin, with dosing continually adjusted using information about meals, exercise, illness, and glucose measurements. We introduce DiabAgent, a research suite for agentic physiological control comprising the Agentic Physiological Control (APC) framework, the DiabetSim simulator, and the SweetBench benchmark. APC controls glucose through medical-device tools, using ongoing observations to infer individual states, accumulate personal experience, and choose treatment actions. We build DiabetSim to simulate different patients, events, and device conditions for scalable virtual testing and training. Using DiabetSim, we construct SweetBench by instantiating 32 scenario designs as 212 glucose-control tasks. With Claude Opus 5.5 and a fixed decision interval of one hour, APC achieves a COGI of 73.5, compared with 71.2 for the open-source closed-loop baseline OpenAPS. Ablations further show that individual adaptation and contextual information improve glucose control. Combining high-frequency rule-based control with lower-frequency agent decisions shows potential for balancing control performance and computational cost. Our work provides a framework, simulator, and evaluation foundation for agents to participate in human physiological control.

title: Raman Spectroscopy for Glioma Diagnosis Toward Precision Neuro-Oncology: A Systematic Review.
desc: [Critical reviews in oncology/hematology] Gliomas are the most common primary malignant tumors of the central nervous system and remain difficult to manage because of diffuse infiltration and molecular heterogeneity. As glioma classification increasingly relies on molecular biomarkers, interest has grown in label-free technologies capable of providing real-time biochemical information during surgery. Although Raman spectroscopy has emerged as a promising optical approach, its diagnostic performance and translational readiness remain incompletely defined. This systematic review was registered in PROSPERO and conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for studies published between 2015 and 2025 evaluating Raman-based technologies for glioma diagnosis. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment using QUADAS-2. Owing to methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized using a SWiM-guided narrative approach. Forty-seven studies met the eligibility criteria. Across conventional Raman spectroscopy, surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy, stimulated Raman histology, stimulated Raman scattering, and multimodal platforms, Raman-based technologies consistently demonstrated strong performance for tissue discrimination, tumor margin assessment, molecular characterization, and intraoperative tissue evaluation. Recent studies increasingly integrated artificial intelligence for automated tissue classification and molecular prediction. However, substantial heterogeneity in acquisition protocols, analytical workflows, and validation strategies, together with predominantly retrospective single-center studies and limited external validation, reduced confidence in clinical generalizability. QUADAS-2 identified the greatest risk of bias in the patient-selection and index-test domains. Raman spectroscopy is evolving from an optical imaging technique into a molecular decision-support platform for precision neuro-oncology. Future clinical translation will depend on methodological standardization, prospective multicenter validation, explainable artificial intelligence, and integration into routine neurosurgical workflows.

title: Attention Residual U-Net for Enhanced Cross-Dataset Polyp Localization in Endoscopy
desc: Precise localization of pathologies in endoscopy is a critical task in medical imaging, with deep learning (DL) frameworks now serving as the primary methodology for automated lesion detection. Today, generic object detection methods, such as YOLO, provide state-of-the-art performance in this context. However, their robustness often decreases under real-world clinical conditions due to variations across endoscopic devices, intestinal content, dataset bias, and the presence of small or low-contrast lesions. Motivated by these challenges, we propose a novel polyp detection framework based on a Attention Residual U-Net offering enhanced polyp localization. Instead of directly regressing bounding boxes from global feature representations, the proposed method learns lesion-focused spatial representations and converts them into bounding-box predictions during inference. Unlike conventional encoder-decoder localization frameworks that directly propagate all encoder activations into the decoding pathway, the proposed method selectively suppresses irrelevant background responses before feature reconstruction. This encourages the network to focus on lesion-relevant spatial evidence under heterogeneous imaging conditions. To achieve this, the framework integrates residual feature propagation, attention-guided encoder filtering, and multi-scale contextual learning. The proposed framework was evaluated on multiple public endoscopic datasets acquired using different devices. The comparative experimental results validate its effectiveness over the relevant state-of-the-art methods, with an improvement up to 22.0% in terms of the area under the receiving operating characteristic (AUC).

title: Artificial intelligence for ophthalmic vessel segmentation: from multimodal imaging to clinical translation.
desc: [Frontiers in medicine] Artificial intelligence (AI)-based vessel segmentation converts color fundus photographs, scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (SLO), optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), structural OCT, and anterior-segment images into quantitative vascular biomarkers. Strong performance within individual datasets has not consistently yielded reliable clinical measurements because errors can arise during acquisition, anatomical preprocessing, vessel extraction, biomarker calculation, and deployment. This structured narrative review compares segmentation tasks involving retinal vascular trees, OCTA capillary plexuses, the structural choroid and choriocapillaris, macular neovascularization, corneal neovascularization, and conjunctival microvasculature. We assess modern architectures in relation to vessel geometry, severe foreground-background imbalance, scale variation, crossings, and susceptibility to artifacts. The methods considered include multiscale feature pyramids, deformable and directional operators, Transformers, state-space models, diffusion approaches, and foundation models. We organize the synthesis around five evaluation levels: pixel overlap, centerline recovery, vascular topology, biomarker agreement, and clinical actionability. Public fundus and OCTA datasets are catalogued with their acquisition and annotation characteristics, and gaps in public anterior-segment vessel benchmarks are discussed. Because devices, data splits, labels, and post-processing differ substantially, reported metrics are summarized without ranking studies against one another. The review distinguishes structural OCT choroidal vascularity index from OCTA choriocapillaris flow-deficit mapping, as well as true vessel segmentation from global hyperemia grading. Clinical translation will require ocular-magnification correction, quality control of retinal layers and projection artifacts, external testing across devices and populations, out-of-distribution rejection, DICOM/PACS interoperability, prospective impact studies, and regulation as software as a medical device. We conclude that clinical utility depends on an auditable pipeline that measures structural error, biomarker uncertainty, and failure states throughout the workflow.

title: Measuring AI Agents as Teammates with Collaborative Intelligence
desc: Progress in AI is often measured by what a single model can do on its own. Yet teams of AI agents are starting to make breakthroughs and discoveries in science, medicine, mathematics and software engineering. As AI begins to work in teams of agents and people, the ability to collaborate becomes a core part of their intelligence. Research on human teams has measured this ability for decades. Inspired by this, we introduce the Collaborative Intelligence Benchmark, which measures how well an AI agent works as a teammate. It contains 240 tasks across 8 dimensions of teamwork, from refusing an unsafe shortcut to checking the work that a weaker model leaves behind. Each task comes from a real record or an existing benchmark, from aviation accident reports and clinical cases to coding tasks and negotiations, and has a programmatically verifiable outcome. To isolate teamwork from individual capability, models are scored only on tasks that they can solve by themselves when they have full information. We evaluate 18 closed- and open-weight models and find that every model, across sizes and families, has clear weaknesses as a teammate, with the best model scoring only 82.2 out of 100. Frontier models almost always refuse unsafe shortcuts and report misconduct, yet they cave under interpersonal pressure, reaching the best overall deal in only 14% of conflicts, and their pass rate drops from 97% to 81% when they take over a task in which a weaker model has cheated. Crucially, general capability does not guarantee good teamwork, as models with nearly the same capability score differ by up to 11 points as teammates. The benchmark includes 160 public tasks with code and data, along with 80 held-out tasks for evaluation. As AI agents increasingly work alongside other agents and people, the ability to collaborate effectively is becoming a crucial capability to measure and develop.

title: Fungal-bacterial interactions.
desc: [Current biology : CB] The study of fungal-bacterial interactions is an emerging field of biology with relevance for environmental health, medicine, and agriculture, among other sectors. The frequent co-occurrence of fungi and bacteria in many habitats has facilitated the evolution of their symbioses. Both groups are key players in host-associated microbiomes and in nutrient cycling, and these roles often intersect in dynamic ways. Interactions between fungi and bacteria can be mutualistic, commensal, or pathogenic, and they can vary in a context-dependent manner. In mutualistic interactions, fungi and bacteria can exchange nutrients, ameliorate each other's stress, enhance growth, enable dispersal, and facilitate novel niche exploration via metabolite exchange. In contrast, antagonistic interactions frequently involve competition for limited nutrients, such as iron, and active chemical warfare with secreted and bioactive compounds. Bacteria associated with fungi can occur inside of fungal cells (endosymbiotic) or on the surface of fungal hyphae (exosymbiotic). Endosymbiotic bacteria can be further differentiated into facultative symbionts, which retain the ability to enter fungal hyphae but also live independently, and obligate endosymbionts, which are always intracellular and not capable of independent life outside of hyphae. Whereas free-living bacteria can be pathogenic or mutualistic, endosymbiotic bacteria are often regarded as commensals or mutualists, although some can exhibit parasitic attributes in some conditions. A combination of molecular genetics, genomics, and microscopy has been used to study free-living bacteria. In addition to these approaches, fluorescence and electron microscopy have been used as the gold standards to study and differentiate endosymbiotic bacteria based on their intracellular location. More recently, researchers have started using systems-biology approaches to study fungal-bacterial interactions including high-throughput -omics assays. These methods produce expansive datasets that are ideally suited to artificial intelligence (AI)-based approaches to tackle long-standing questions about the basic biology and evolution of fungal-bacterial interactions. In this primer we give an overview of fungal-bacterial interactions, including their diversity, community structure, and symbiotic evolution. We highlight two research systems in particular: the intracellular endosymbionts of Mucoromycota fungi and the free-living bacteria associated with edible

title: SMILE: A Structured Multi-Agent Clinical Reasoning for Liver Ultrasound Understanding
desc: Automated liver ultrasound report generation improves the diagnosis of liver diseases by producing clinically structured descriptions of anatomical and disease-related findings. However, current generative vision-language models (VLMs) often rely on a single reasoning pathway that maps ultrasound appearance directly to textual descriptions. In addition to the inherent vision-language modality gap, this design is limited for liver ultrasound because disease interpretation is constrained by subtle visual evidence, heterogeneous disease patterns, and limited paired supervision. To address these limitations, we propose SMILE, a Structured Multi-agent clInicaL rEasoning framework that uses multiple complementary specialist agents to interpret ultrasound images and consolidates their outputs through a judge-guided consensus mechanism. Our approach employs three specialized agents: an image interpretation agent for morphological descriptions, a clinical-stage reasoning agent, and a visual question answering (VQA) agent for targeted queries. These agent responses are then aggregated and scrutinized by a judge VLM using a consensus filtering prompt to produce a unified, clinically coherent output. Across a public liver ultrasound dataset and an internal clinical dataset, SMILE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art VLMs, achieving up to 19.0\% improvement in ROUGE-1 and 18.8\% improvement in clinical F1-score, while reaching VQA F1-scores of 0.82 and 0.65 on public and internal datasets, respectively. These results demonstrate the potential of SMILE for data-scarce and limited-supervision clinical settings. Our models, datasets, and code are available \href{https://github.com/CMME-Lab/SMILE}{here}.

title: Reducing radiographic retake rates with ultra-low dose pre-shots using deep learning-based noise reduction: A prospective clinical study.
desc: [Radiography (London, England : 1995)] The pre-shot technique is an effective approach to lower retake radiography rates; however, it is limited by increased patient radiation exposure. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of an ultra-low-dose pre-shot enabled by deep learning-based noise reduction (Advanced Intelligent Clear-IQ Engine: AiCE) on reducing retake rates in wrist radiography. A CXDI-810C (Canon Medical Systems) was used as the X-ray detector. Phantom images simulating lateral wrist pre-shots with and without AiCE were acquired under fixed imaging conditions using an additional 1.0 mm copper filter. The tube current-time product was reduced from 2.8 mAs to 0.5 mAs. Fifteen radiological technologists determined the optimal imaging condition using a five-point confidence scale, with scores below three considered insufficient for retake decision-making. A prospective clinical evaluation was then conducted, comparing retake rates between a non-pre-shot group (n = 542) and a pre-shot group (n = 325). The entrance surface air kerma (Ka,e) was estimated from phantom measurements. Without AiCE, no imaging condition met the threshold required for retake decision-making. Conversely, with AiCE, a tube current-time product of 1.6 mAs achieved acceptable image quality (3.29 ± 0.47), with all evaluators assigning scores ≥3; therefore, it was selected as the optimal condition. In the clinical evaluation, the retake rate markedly decreased from 14.38% to 0.61%. The pre-shot Ka,e was 0.11 ± 0.03 μGy, corresponding to only 0.15% of the standard lateral wrist radiography dose. AiCE-enabled ultra-low-dose pre-shot imaging dramatically reduced retake rates while requiring minimal additional radiation dose. The ultra-low-dose pre-shot using AiCE represents a highly effective strategy to minimize retake imaging with negligible dose penalty, offering substantial potential for dose optimization and improved workflow efficiency in clinical radiography.

title: When Prediction Shapes the Future: A BlueSky Agenda for Reflexive Time Series Analysis
desc: Time-series models are increasingly deployed in operational systems (e.g., inventory management and clinical care) where predictions trigger interventions that alter future observations, producing records we term AI-shaped trajectories. This sequence-prediction coupling deepens as such systems evolve into agents that autonomously predict, act, and remember across long horizons. Such AI-shaped trajectories support immediate performance monitoring, but turn ambiguous once reused as passive data. An algorithm may then misread a prediction-prevented stockout as naturally stable demand, or an averted medical crisis as a false alarm. This ambiguity then propagates into everything built on the record, from retraining and agent memory to downstream predictive tasks. As a result, systems may internalize these intervention effects as natural phenomena, drifting further from the truth at every closed-loop cycle. In this Blue Sky paper, we advocate an agenda for reflexive time-series analysis that shifts the analytical object from the intervention-agnostic sequence to the prediction-action-observation loop. The agenda requires closed-loop provenance to track the operational context (e.g., predictions, policies, and actions), sequence identification to estimate how those actions affect future values under explicit causal assumptions, and closed-loop evaluation to separate intrinsic process prediction from policy-driven effects. This foundation is essential for integrating autonomous agents into such loops at scale, enabling the joint learning of intervention effects and intrinsic dynamics for robust temporal representations.

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Developing a Future-Ready Nursing Workforce: A Systematic Review.
desc: [Journal of nursing management] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming health care through advanced technologies that support clinical practice, education, workforce management, and decision making. As healthcare systems face growing challenges related to workforce shortages, increasing service demands, and rapid digital transformation, there is a need to understand how AI can contribute to the development of a future-ready nursing workforce equipped with the competencies required for modern healthcare environments. This systematic review aimed to examine the role of AI in developing a future-ready nursing workforce and to synthesize current evidence regarding its applications, benefits, challenges, and implications for workforce preparedness. A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and was registered in PROSPERO. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, and IEEE Xplore were searched for studies published between January 2015 and February 2026. Eligible primary studies examined an identifiable AI technology or an AI-specific construct in nursing education, clinical practice, workforce development, competency development, workforce planning, or professional preparedness. Methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, and findings were synthesized narratively. A total of 38 primary empirical studies satisfied the AI-specific eligibility criteria. The evidence was concentrated in cross-sectional (n = 15) and qualitative (n = 11) designs, with fewer development/prototype (n = 6), mixed methods (n = 3), randomized or quasi-experimental (n = 2), and methodological (n = 1) studies. AI-supported education, clinical decision support, workforce forecasting, and competency development showed promising benefits, but much of the evidence was based on perceptions, simulations, prototypes, or single-site evaluations rather than long-term implementation. Recurrent barriers included limited AI literacy, ethical and privacy concerns, algorithmic bias, infrastructure constraints, workflow integration, and organizational readiness. AI has promising, but still uneven, potential to support a future-ready nursing workforce. Current evidence supports cautious and staged integration rather than uncritical scale-up. Standardized AI and digital competency frameworks, human oversight, governance, infrastructure readiness, and prospective evaluation of effectiveness, equity, and cost are needed before widespread deployment.
